items.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was playing opposite Louis Armstrong at the Basin Street

ctx.x: Yeah. I remember a conversation, I was playing opposite Louis Armstrong at the Basin Street, Tristano came in and [he] was having a big conversation I found later, talking about Louis Armstrong being sharp, the last thing anybody said about Louis Armstrong. And, you know, cultivating a young alto player who played sharp, it seemed strange.
Well, you’re never too old to get a new accusation, apparently at the age of eighty-three somebody’s telling you that you play flat.
